course_name_original: Introduction au calcul différentiel et à l'algèbre linéaire
course_name_en: Introduction to Differential Calculus and Linear Algebra
prerequisites: Concepts from the course 'Algebra tools for sciences' from UE 4 in S1 (linear systems, vector spaces, dimension).
Concepts from UE 3 in S1 (limits, Landau notation, continuity, derivation).

learning_outcomes.text: Recognize the linearity of an application and determine its matrix in a basis.
Mobilize mathematical concepts to approach and solve problems with a high level of abstraction.
Identify a problem within a disciplinary field.
Analyze a problem by mobilizing disciplinary concepts.
Acquire the techniques of primitive calculation.
Understand the local behavior of a function by polynomial approximation.
Apply Taylor series expansions to calculations of limits, asymptotes, and the search for local extrema.
Manipulate the main mathematical tools useful in physics.
Implement methods and tools from the disciplinary field.

syllabus_topics: Linear applications: definition, image and kernel, rank theorem.
Matrix algebra: operations on matrices, matrix of a linear application, change of basis matrix, invertible matrix. Gauss-Jordan method for inverting a square matrix.
Primitive calculations: primitives of usual functions, integration by parts, change of variable.
Higher-order derivatives: definition, Leibniz formula, convexity, Taylor-Young formula (admitted).
Taylor series expansions: definition, operations, Taylor series expansions of usual functions, application to limit calculations, local extrema, and asymptotes.
